summary: User's call after MPI-465: we should test that all workflows still run every time ComfyUI is bumped, as part of a bump skill or playbook, creating one if it does not exist. Confirmed it does not - mpi-bump-local-comfy bumps only the BENCH at G:/ComfyUi, the engine core pin in node_lock.json has no skill and no playbook, and no test ever executes a workflow (tests/ has only workflow-input-staging-gate). The user flagged the obvious blocker himself: he cannot have every model installed at once. The answer is that he does not need to - smoke what IS installed locally (LTX is, which is exactly what would have caught MPI-465) and put the full matrix on the Builder Pod, whose volume already owns the weights. Note for whoever builds it: a validation-only pass is NOT sufficient - MPI-465 threw at sampling start after the loaders ran, so validation would have passed it green.

Scope stated explicitly (playbook + smoke runner + release gate; the mechanic is MPI-457) and dispatch notes added to brief.md: named home for the runner, the tier/step budget question, the one-GPU serialization constraint, and the fact that LTX cannot be smoked locally until MPI-466 ships - which is exactly the case the never-report-green-for-an-unrun-model rule exists for.

Implementation started. Plan approved by the user 2026-08-07. Design settled in-session: the smoke runs on a RunPod GPU Pod in EU-RO-1 off a SEPARATE 320GB network volume, not locally - one GPU here and it is busy, and a local run can never hold every weight, which is exactly the silent-skip failure MPI-465 shipped. Card order L4 -> RTX 3090 -> RTX 4090, first available. Runner drives the running app on :3000 because every route already exists (/runpod/gpu-availability, volume CRUD, /remote/*), so it writes no new API code and exercises the path users hit. Execution unit is the OP (~35), not the workflow file (12) - klein-4b alone runs 7 branches through one graph. Minimization is generic by node TITLE (Input_Width/Height/Steps/Frames), never a per-graph table. Smoke set is deduped by class_type SET (a bump breaks a node) at the lowest tier per family: 12 graphs / 312.2GB today, 285.1GB once Wan t2v is deprecated, ~281GB once LTX is int8 at 21GB - both in flight in other sessions, so the runner RECOMPUTES from the registry and hardcodes nothing.

MPI-468 SPLIT CHANGED, recorded on both cards as the umbrella brief requires. The bump SKILL now EXISTS as /mpi-bump-engine, created under MPI-467 because routing was the gap the user hit: a cold agent told "test all the models" had no path to the playbook and would have grabbed /mpi-bump-local-comfy, which is BENCH-only. It follows the repo pattern (/mpi-add-model enforces add-model/, /mpi-add-flow enforces add-flow/). MPI-457 must EXTEND that skill with the in-place mechanic - git fetch --tags + checkout the pinned sha + pip only the changed core packages + restamp .mpi_engine_version - and the gate-5 empirical class_type check. It must NOT create a second bump skill: one skill, one playbook. That collision is the whole reason MPI-468 exists.

validation.md written: what ran (self-check with negative controls, --plan at 11 models / 34 ops / 279.5GB, the release gate proven in all four branches, suite 478/478) and what did NOT (live GPU survey, and the entire live half - volume/CPU install/version assert/dispatch).

Implementation complete and verified: playbook, runner, enforced release gate, /mpi-bump-engine skill. Outstanding is the LIVE proving run only - create the 320GB EU-RO-1 volume, fill ~281GB on a CPU Pod, rent L4/3090/4090, execute all 34 ops. The live GPU survey also never ran (app was not up on :3000). Schedule the proving run AFTER H3/LTX/Wan settle - the smoke set is resolved from the registry at run time, so smoking now measures a moving target, and the run doubles as the remote-half verification for those cards.

Two defects in --models, fixed in 51dc080e, found while the user asked whether a release can skip models. (1) The flag NEVER RAN: resolveSmokeSet returned early on the scoped branch and skipped the tail that computes totalGb/depIds/skippedWeights, so printPlan died on set.totalGb.toFixed(1). Both branches now share one tail. (2) A scoped run wrote evidence indistinguishable from the full matrix - 7 pass / 0 fail - because checkSmokeEvidence reads only engine version, fail count and staleness. The runner refuses to fold an in-run SKIP into the pass count; a model excluded by --models never became a result row at all, the same lie one level up. evidence.scope now carries requested/modelsRun/covers/unproven/modelsInRegistry; --plan prints the unproven list BEFORE anything is rented; release:check REPORTS coverage and does not gate on it (the user explicitly chose to leave the gate engine-pin-only). A scoped set is deliberately not deduped, so covers is empty and --models sdxl-realistic proves nothing about its four siblings. Verified: --plan --models klein-4b prints 18 of 19 unproven, the full --plan prints no scope warning, all three release:check branches exercised by probe evidence files (written, run, removed). Suite 482/482.

Release-gate scope decided by the user and NOT widened: checkSmokeEvidence stays engine-pin-only (release-health-check.mjs:448). Known hole, deliberately accepted - a release that bumps only a node pin does NOT owe smoke evidence, which is the exact shape of MPI-465s own fix commit c077efa9 (it moved a nodes[].commit and left comfyui.core.tag alone). Same for adding a model. Widening the trigger would cost a ~281GB volume fill plus a GPU hour on every node bump; the user will drive the smoke by hand per version instead. Revisit only if a node-bump release ships broken. The floor check (scripts/engine-floor-check.mjs) is also NOT in release:check - it needs a live engine on 48188 and CI has none; wiring it would need its own evidence file.

Gate 6 complete: pod node_lock+python_deps synced to ComfyUI 0.30.0 (mpi-ci b6fa6c5, 4d02e27); DEV image v0.20.0-dev built both legs in run 31157902185, pull-verified, node-import smoke OK, cpu boot-smoked wrapper 0.2.41; POD_IMAGE_VERSION_DEV/_CPU_DEV bumped (13e34c31), stable pair untouched at v0.17.0. Gates 7-9 deferred until H3 reference-to-video lands.

Healed three gaps found by walking the playbook for real (a2b677f3): the pod drift check compared node_lock only and missed python_deps.txt; gate 6 documented a lock-only sync; build-pod-image 5b could not see the baked wrapper because bootstrap unsets the baked env after fetching the R2 channel. The new check immediately caught real drift - MPI-472 added imageio-ffmpeg after the pod sync, so the v0.20.0-dev image lacks it and needs a rebuild before the smoke.

Handoff c3a71f04 written for a fresh session. MPI-467 is the 1.4 blocker and the only one: release:check fails solely on the missing smoke-evidence.json. The handoff leads with the prerequisite the --plan run reports (the Pod lock is behind on python_deps.txt, so smoking now measures the old engine), then the DEV-tag-only image build, then the smoke run itself.

Resumed for the live proving run. Pod python_deps drift closed WITHOUT an image rebuild (mpi-ci 27087c2): MpiNodes find_ffmpeg falls back to shutil.which and both Dockerfiles apt-install ffmpeg, so MPI-472 imageio-ffmpeg is a Windows-portable-only fix and v0.20.0-dev stays current. Then three runner faults fixed before any spend (f1df91fa) - no CPU download Pod created (installs would have gone to the LOCAL disk), a Windows probe path injected into MpiLoadImageFromPath which resolves on the Pod, and an install wait that ignored installing/paused and never checked for failed deps. Added a free offline preflight of every op to --plan: 35/35 resolve a graph, a branch and a budget.

Live run attempted 3x, never reached the GPU stage. Six runner faults found by reading the routes and fixed: no CPU download Pod (installs would have gone to the LOCAL disk), a Windows probe path injected into a Pod-side loader, an install wait blind to installing/paused and to failures, a cold Pod 404 window that killed all 12 LTX deps, all 13 models POSTed at once (63 concurrent installs starved the Pod into 524-ing /health for 90 min), and a bare-array response that minted a new 350 GB volume per run (three existed). Added a Pod-boot budget with host recycling and a no-bytes-moved stall detector, so the next run does not need a human on the RunPod console. ~97 GB down on volume aghcuvg7nl. Handoff c4efc95b-54d4-4bbf-bdfd-cab1cf13017c written.

OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED - it is the DATACENTER, not the image. The handoff left it undecided whether EU-RO-1 was broken on the night of 2026-08-08 or whether something about this image/volume combination provokes the container's 'network must exist' loop. Run 2 settled it: attempts 1 and 2 both hit the 5-minute boot ceiling and were recycled, attempt 3 came up and installed - all three on the SAME image (ghcr.io/madponyinteractive/cubric-vision-pod:v0.20.0-dev-cpu), the same runtime channel (dev), the same volume (aghcuvg7nl) and the same cpu3c flavor. An image or runtime fault cannot succeed on the third identical try, so the missing-cpu-tag and broken-dev-runtime hypotheses are DISPROVEN. Five dead CPU hosts across two sessions is EU-RO-1 host flakiness, and the volume is DC-locked there, so the answer is the recycle watchdog rather than a move. The watchdog (e60b269b) fired twice unattended in this run - its first real firings, and both correct. Practical note for the next run: budget for 2-3 wasted Pod boots (~5 min each) before the fill starts; that is normal here, not a fault to debug.

STANDING CONSTRAINT from the user 2026-08-08: DO NOT DELETE network volume aghcuvg7nl (cubric-smoke, 350 GB, EU-RO-1) when the smoke run finishes. It is no longer just a cost-vs-refill tradeoff - he needs the installed model set intact to record YouTube videos, and wants AS MANY MODELS INSTALLED AS POSSIBLE kept on it. Refilling is not a pennies-and-hours inconvenience here, it blocks content work. The current run is already safe: --keep-volume skips the teardown branch in smoke-workflows.mjs entirely, so only the Pod is deleted. The exposure is a FUTURE run invoked WITHOUT the flag - it prompts 'Delete the volume? [y/N]', and an agent answering 'y' destroys the set. ALWAYS pass --keep-volume --volume aghcuvg7nl, and never answer that prompt affirmatively without asking him first. Deleting a Pod is fine and expected; deleting the volume is not.

GPU LEG REVIEWED BEFORE IT EVER RAN - three findings, one patched. (1) PATCHED, a money leak: the GPU Pod was created with a bare /remote/pod/create + a hard 20-minute waitReady, and die() is process.exit(1) which deletes NOTHING. A dead host would have cost 20 idle minutes and then LEAKED a rented GPU Pod, billing until a human noticed. The CPU leg has been immune since e60b269b only because createPodWithRetry deletes the Pod before every retry AND before giving up. Routed the GPU create through the same helper, 2 attempts not 3 because each attempt is billed GPU time. node --check passes. NOT applied to the in-flight run - node loaded the .mjs at startup, so the running process keeps the old code; the next relaunch picks it up. (2) NOT A BUG, checked rather than assumed: /runpod/gpu-availability returns {gpuTypes:[...]}, so pickGpu's destructure is correct and fault 6's bare-array trap does NOT repeat here. (3) UNFIXED, two soft spots worth a hardening pass. The response has NO stockStatus field at all, so pickGpu's guard `g.stockStatus == null || ...` can never fire - it is a watcher armed on a condition nothing produces, and the runner therefore never actually checks stock. RunPod's real availability signal in this payload looks like lowestPrice.minMemory being non-null (MI300X shows nulls, L4/3090/4090 show 55/30/31). Separately the name match is a loose substring: 'L4' also matches L40 and L40S, and 'RTX 3090' also matches 3090 Ti, so a pricier card can be selected silently - L4 happens to sort first in the array today, which is luck, not logic. OWED: fold all of this into docs/playbooks/bump-engine/01-smoke-run.md with the other faults.

Handoff 6e987efc-0ecd-43d8-bc6a-f80fce853c6d written. Fill halted at 8/12 installed on the grown 450 GB volume with model 9 resumable - stopped by decision, not fault: HuggingFace throttles the H3 weights to a measured 1.66 MB/s mean, a ~10-hour tail. Pod deleted, jobs cleared, nothing running. Four more runner faults fixed this session (eb89f59f), the EU-RO-1 question answered, and the GPU leg still never executed.

THE RUNNER AND THE RELEASE GATE DEADLOCKED - found by reading, before renting anything, and it would have wasted the whole GPU matrix. assertPodEngineVersion read status.comfyVersion off /remote/comfy/status, a field that route has never returned (it answers running, ready, comfyReady, wrapperVersion, connecting, connectElapsedMs, noGpu) and the wrapper /health only adds wrapper_version. So got was always the empty string, the mismatch die() was unreachable, and the run would write engine.got null - which release-health-check.mjs checkSmokeEvidence then REFUSES for not proving what was smoked. A full matrix could not produce evidence its own gate accepts. Fixed by reading manifest.comfyui_ref, the only record of the ref a Pod image was built from, through a new /remote/pod/manifest passthrough; no comfyui_ref now STOPS the run rather than spending on a rejected file, with --allow-unproven-engine as the escape hatch for an unbumped run. SECOND FAULT, same class as eb89f59f but downstream of it: die() is process.exit(1) and deletes nothing, so every failure AFTER a successful create still leaked the rental - engine mismatch, probe upload, any app() 502, any throw into main().catch. abort() now deletes the live Pod first and every post-create exit routes through it. Verified: route registered and guarding (409 remote_inactive on a 3999 harness, unknown paths still 404), runner self-check green. NOT yet verified against a live Pod - the route is in routes/, so it is inert until the app restarts, same as MPI-481. Playbook third-pass section written. Peer MPI-491 cleared the Gate E download blocker: all five H3 deps are installed via hf_xet, and controlnet-union-flux is the one HF dep left uninstalled - it is the clean GPU-image test of _download_hf they asked for.
